transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because something at work really scared me. I work in surveillance, and during the quiet stretches I’ve been hearing voices through the monitor speakers saying things like, “You missed it, Ruth,” or, “People are going to get hurt because of you.” But the channels are muted, and no one else hears it.
Have you heard these voices outside of work, or when you aren't near the monitors?

No, not really. It’s been in the surveillance room, during the quiet stretches, like it’s coming through the monitor speakers. That’s what scared me, because the channels were muted and nobody else heard anything.
Have you been feeling unusually down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… most days I wake up and it’s like this heavy gray feeling is already there before I even get out of bed. I’ve been tearing up in my car before my shift sometimes, just seeing the casino lights, and I don’t even know why.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, activities, or even spending time with people?

Yeah. I used to actually look forward to things—salsa class, softball, building PCs, having people over for board games. Lately I just ignore the texts and stay home. It’s like none of it can really reach me.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic, happy, or irritable for several days in a row, where you needed less sleep or felt like your thoughts were racing?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t had stretches where I felt really energized or unusually happy like that. If anything, I’ve been more worn down than anything else.
Have you ever had experiences where you saw, heard, or believed something that others around you didn’t, outside of the voices you heard at work?

Not really outside of that. The main thing is in the surveillance room, when it gets quiet, I’ll hear voices coming through the monitor speakers. They’ll say things like, “You missed it, Ruth,” or “People are going to get hurt because of you.” But the channels are muted, and when I ask, nobody else hears it. It scared me enough that I knew I needed to come in.
Have there been times when you believed something strongly that others around you didn't agree with or thought wasn't true?

Yeah… I guess so. I keep thinking every missed camera angle or slow call I’ve made is proof that I’m careless, like I’m dangerous in that job. Other people tell me I’m being too hard on myself, but it feels true to me. Part of me feels like if something goes wrong while I’m on watch, I deserve to be punished for it.
Do you believe that your thoughts about being careless and dangerous are true, even though others tell you otherwise?

Yes… most of the time I do believe it. I know people say I’m being too hard on myself, but I keep going back over every camera angle I missed or any call I made too late, and it feels like proof that I’m careless. Like I’m dangerous to have in that position. And if something bad happens while I’m on watch, part of me feels like I deserve to be punished for it.
When you think that you're dangerous and deserve punishment, does it feel like a gut instinct or something your mind logically figures out, even if others don't see it that way?

It feels like my mind is figuring it out from what happened. Like I replay the camera angles I missed or the calls I made late, and it adds up as proof that I’m careless. And then it feels true that I’m dangerous in that job… and if something goes wrong while I’m watching, I deserve to be punished for it.
Do these thoughts about being dangerous and deserving punishment ever go away completely, or do they feel like a constant truth to you, even when you're not feeling down?

No… they weren’t always there. Before this whole stretch, when I started feeling so hopeless and guilty after the lead change in surveillance, I didn’t think like this. I wasn’t hearing accusations through the equipment, and I didn’t feel so sure I was dangerous to everyone.

It feels like the voices and these beliefs are tied to this low period. They don’t feel like something that was always true about me.
When you hear the voices or think that you’re dangerous and deserve punishment, do these thoughts fit with how you’ve been feeling emotionally, or do they feel separate from your mood?

They fit with how I’ve been feeling. Before this stretch, when I got so hopeless and guilty after the surveillance lead change, I wasn’t hearing accusations through the equipment, and I didn’t feel so sure I was dangerous to everyone.

It all seems tied together… the voices, the guilt, the belief that I deserve punishment. It doesn’t feel separate from my mood.
